entries.positive_observation: The final derivative retains the approved parent RGB art: an uncovered compact rounded mascot head remains almost wholly black with only a thin crown/side rim light and one faint closed mouth; no green eyes, human nose, human skin or human ears are newly exposed, and no headgear was added. The dark uniform retains pale shoulder edges, two light-embroidered dark collar patch groups, a grey shirt and one dark tie in the original subdued lighting. The near-frontal slight image-left pose, shoulder/chest crop, continuous pale grey-beige backing, central muted halo and darker vignette remain recognizable. The rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a long neck, pinching, floating cloth or cream bib. No frame or note was invented. Full white/cyan/alpha viewing shows complete backing and clothing without holes, smoke or a working-matte halo.
entries.alpha_decision: Accept the repaired RGBA for production. Independent read-only verification confirms source-alpha-resize-bilinear-rgb-unchanged-v1, identical parent/derived RGB pixels, and output alpha exactly matching the BILINEAR-resized source alpha. Source and returned extrema are [254,255]; source, resized and output corner arrays are all [255,255,255,255]. Actual white/cyan/alpha inspection confirms that the intended near-opaque full-canvas backing remains visually solid with no visible interior transparency or added exterior halo; the measured 254 values were not relabeled 255.
entries.visible_limitations: The exact dark source conceals the precise hairline, sideburns, brows, eyewear, facial hair and gaze, and its tiny collar embroidery cannot be transcribed reliably. No exact hidden-feature or microscopic-insignia match is claimed. Under visible-source-differences-v1 those limits are not rejection grounds; approval rests on the visible silhouette, clothing groups, collar fit, crop and low-key light, including the absence of newly exposed facial features.
